idea_name: Stable profit plateau in 2-param optimization graphs as robustness sensor
mechanism: Optimize pairs of EA parameters and project results onto a 2D profit heat map; prefer contiguous dark (high-profit) regions where neighboring cells show only gradual profit decay over sharp local maxima. Combining pairwise plateaus (e.g. Stoch×RSI, RSI×StopLoss, Stoch×StopLoss) yields a parameter cluster expected to survive small market shifts; reject needle peaks that collapse under tiny parameter moves.
data_needed: Strategy-tester optimization report over ≥2 parameters; pairwise profit grids; optional finer-step re-scan of the chosen cluster
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SP.mq4 demo (RSI/Stochastic/Momentum overbought-oversold EA); Forex example yen/USD; Daily recommended with >3 years sample; out-of-sample holdout
why_new_for_mis: Turns the geometry of the optimization surface into a live robustness/fragility sensor—MIS can flag when a live parameter set sits on a ridge rather than a plateau as market conditions drift.
quote: we search for a hyperplane within which the profit is stable and changes more or less equally when parameters are slightly modified.

idea_name: Daily rolling auto-reoptimization as regime-adaptation sensor
mechanism: At a fixed local time each day, a live Terminal launches a second Terminal-Tester via optimise.ini to reoptimize up to four EA inputs over the last TestDay days; report HTML is parsed, filtered by MinTr/MaxTr trade-count bounds and de-duplicated, then cascaded-sorted by Gross Profit → Profit Factor → Expected Payoff (halving the kept set each pass). Winning parameter vector is written to GlobalVariables and substituted into the live EA—explicitly because Championship evidence showed history-fit EAs lose edge as the market moves, and because which inputs matter most depends on market volatility.
data_needed: Duplicate MT4 install; .set of optimizable inputs; daily tester HTML reports; GlobalVariables bridge; stable 24h connection
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; MACD Sample_1 (FastEMA, SlowEMA, SignalSMA); TestDay=3 demo window
why_new_for_mis: Frames scheduled rolling reoptimization itself as a change sensor: parameter jumps and fitness collapse across daily windows mark regime breaks MIS can watch without a separate classifier.
quote: it is better to use this automated optimizer to fit parameters of the variables the changes in which influence the EA operation more than those in other variables, depending on the market volatility.

idea_name: Cross-pair correlation coefficient as hedge-regime sensor
mechanism: Define hedge pairs by empirical correlation: +1 same-direction (e.g. buy EURUSD / sell GBPUSD), −1 opposite-direction (e.g. buy EURUSD / buy USDCHF), 0 random. Because correlation is not constant and one leg often lags the other (rabbit/turtle delay), the overlap window is where hedgers extract profit—export daily opens and hourly ticks of both legs, virtualize combined PnL, and treat correlation sign/strength (and its breakdown) as the regime that justifies the hedge.
data_needed: Synchronized OHLC/ticks for both symbols; optional rolling correlation series; lot sizes and contract sizes
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Experiment: buy EURJPY 2 lots / sell GBPJPY 1 lot; daily opens + hourly ticks; window 2007.03.17–2007.06.28; also cites EURUSD/GBPUSD and EURUSD/USDCHF
why_new_for_mis: Makes FX cross-correlation (and its non-stationarity/lag) an explicit MIS regime sensor for multi-symbol sleeves, not just a static hedge recipe.
quote: the correlation is not a constant scheme in nature, there will frequently be a delay by one pair, one starts moving, then one will follow after it

idea_name: Relative pair volatility turtle/rabbit lot-ratio sensor
mechanism: When two hedge legs differ in movement capability, size the quieter ('turtle') leg larger and the volatile ('rabbit') leg smaller so adverse rabbit moves are offset by turtle gains; lot ratio is chosen from relative volatility/movement capability before virtual PnL is accumulated from exported ticks.
data_needed: Per-symbol realized range or similar volatility proxy; contract size; account leverage for margin check
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPJPY base 1.0 lot vs EURJPY hedge 2.0 lots in the worked example; hourly tick sampling
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete cross-asset relative-volatility sensor that directly maps into hedge sizing and risk balance.
quote: Lot ratio can lower the risk, affected by more powerful movement pair or rabbit pair, by placing the higher lot size to the turtle pair

idea_name: Bar-range distribution percentile as trailing-distance volatility sensor
mechanism: Mark fixed open/close pattern segments so entry times stay identical across trailing variants; optimize TrailingStop and compare to the empirical bar-size distribution of the test window (ft.BarStat). Optimal trail of 95 points matched the level covering 98% of bars in the period—so the bar-range CDF percentile itself is the volatility sensor that sets a trail distance large enough to survive typical bar noise yet tight enough to lock profit.
data_needed: OHLC bar ranges over the test window; pattern open/close file; trailing variants under test
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 14 pattern buy/sell segments ~2007.11–2008.04 on prices ~1.46–1.58 (EURUSD-like); chart Period() of the marking scripts; TrailingStop optimized to 95 points
why_new_for_mis: Links trailing distance directly to the realized bar-range distribution—MIS can reuse the percentile-of-bar-size as a period volatility gauge for stop/trail policy.
quote: The optimal value producing the largest profit is in good agreement with the bar size statistics of the period under test: 95 points make 98% of all bars of this period

idea_name: Per-block C1–C3 performance over sessions as regime-change sensor
mechanism: Decompose a complex EA into independent signal blocks (A: Parabolic SAR on tf1; B: Accelerator Oscillator on tf2; mode tm=1/2/3 for A-only, B-only, or OR-combined entries). Score each block and the joint system by the same criteria C1 net profit, C2 max drawdown, C3 % profitable trades. Re-measure C1–C3 after time slices (sessions, news) and when a block’s inputs degrade (e.g. SAR tf1 H1→H4): falling block metrics localize which sleeve lost edge and flag a market-condition shift without re-optimizing all nine parameters.
data_needed: Per-block trade logs or isolated backtests; shared criteria vector; optional session/news timestamps
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol generic; module1 PSAR on PERIOD_H1 (Step=0.02, Max=0.2); module2 AC on PERIOD_M5; SL=40 TP=70 demo
why_new_for_mis: Turns modular strategy diagnostics into a MIS change sensor: which signal family is degrading tells when and how the regime moved, enabling targeted re-fit instead of blind global optimization.
quote: The parameters C1-C3 can be measured after some periods of time, thereby clarifying the behavior of the system and its units together and separately at different times of the market (trading sessions, news release, etc.).
